subject: general
question: There are two sections A and B of a class, consisting of 22 and 44 students, respectively. If the average weight of section A is 40 kg and that of section B is 34 kg, find the average weight of the whole class (in kg).
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of student counts in **Section A** and **Section B** = 22 : 44 = **1 : 2**.

Using the **ratio method** for weighted average: [(1 × 40) + (2 × 34)] ÷ (1 + 2).

Combined **average weight** = (40 + 68) ÷ 3 = 108 ÷ 3 = **36 kg**.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 kg.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Students in **Section A** (n₁) = 22 | Average weight (x₁) = 40 kg

Students in **Section B** (n₂) = 44 | Average weight (x₂) = 34 kg

**Formula Used:**

Average weight of the class = (Sum of weights of all students) ÷ (Total number of students)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5aef65a95014fa23fc3c3ac86ef7d000663418457847ffbdef40fe68dbe65845.png] 
⇒ Total weight of **Section A** = 22 × 40 = 880 kg
⇒ Total weight of **Section B** = 44 × 34 = 1496 kg
⇒ **Total class weight** = 880 + 1496 = 2376 kg
⇒ **Total class strength** = 22 + 44 = 66
⇒ **Average weight** of the **whole class** = 2376 ÷ 66 = 36 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 36 kg.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When two groups are combined, the total average is calculated as (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Ratio Simplification

For average weight or score calculations, you can replace actual quantities with their **simplest ratio** to reduce numerical complexity.

Deviation Method

Pick an **assumed average** and calculate the net deviation. The final average is Assumed Average + (Net Deviation ÷ Total Count).</p
